audit.title: Cross-Chain Identity

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong — most sections open with a self-contained definition ("A **Credential Source** is the configuration that tells the `CredentialRegistryIdentityValidatorPolicy` which registries to trust"). No dangling cross-references.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 29 headings, clean H1–H3, 2 comparison tables, no oversized sections.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Mixed. Real specifics exist (`bytes32`, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, tier codes 1/2/3, `common.` namespace), but the facts flag vague quantifiers ("many", "several", "wide range") and 0 numerals carry units. Conceptual page limits numeric opportunity, but the vague quantifiers are replaceable.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 11 links, only 1 external (Wikipedia), **0 to primary sources**. `keccak256`, EVM, and credential-standard claims are unattributed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong. CCID, Credential Source, and type-identifier all have crisp one-sentence definitions near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak per measured facts — no JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no head date, no og/twitter tags. Largely site-level, but it caps agent trust and freshness signals.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 2 fenced blocks, both **untagged**, both one-liners (`keccak256(...)`). No `solidity` language hint; no runnable example of `registerIdentity()` / `registerCredential()` despite being named in prose.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good lifecycle and "why" coverage (Design rationale answers "why CCID", "why offchain"). Missing explicit FAQ/troubleshooting and symptom-phrased entry points.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent entity naming (CCID, Credential Issuer, IdentityRegistry) aids entity resolution.

audit.summary: This is a well-structured conceptual page explaining Chainlink ACE's Cross-Chain Identity model, with strong answer-first definitions and clean chunking (29 sections, median 45 words, zero level skips). Its single biggest strength is quotable canonical definitions ("A **CCID** is a `bytes32` value that represents a single identity across all EVM blockchains"). Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability: the served page carries **zero JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no head-level date** despite a body "Last Updated" line — invisible metadata that weakens agent trust. Honest verdict: solid, retrievable conceptual doc that leaves easy GEO lift on the table in metadata, code tagging, and symptom-phrased query coverage.

recommendations.title: Add page-level JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema with canonical + dates
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `dateModified: 2026-07-17` (mirror the visible "Last Updated"), `inLanguage: en`, and a `canonical` URL. Surface the date in head, not just body prose.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness are direct E-E-A-T / "API-able" signals engines use to rank and trust sources.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: new section near "Credential lifecycle" or end of page
recommendations.issue: headings are concept-titled ("The registry model"); devs query by task/symptom.
recommendations.change: Add H3s phrased as queries: "How do I verify a KYC credential across chains?", "How do I require credentials from two providers?", "Why is my credential validation failing after expiration?" — each with a 2–3 sentence answer-first block.
recommendations.why: Symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the answer is already in body text.

recommendations.title: Tag code fences and add a runnable registration snippet
recommendations.where: the `keccak256(...)` blocks and the lifecycle steps naming `registerIdentity()` / `registerCredential()`
recommendations.change: Tag existing fences as `solidity`; add one complete, labeled snippet showing a `registerIdentity()` / `registerCredential()` call with parameter names, credential type, and expiration.
recommendations.why: Labeled, complete snippets are copy-pasteable by coding agents and raise extraction confidence.

recommendations.title: Add inline citations to primary sources
recommendations.where: "type identifier … generated by hashing a namespaced string" (`keccak256`)
recommendations.change: Link `keccak256` to the Ethereum/Solidity docs, and link "EVM chains" to a canonical network reference. Keep the existing ISO 3166 link.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with concrete specifics
recommendations.where: Design rationale ("supporting a wide range of credential formats"); Credential Sources ("several sources")
recommendations.issue: "vague quantifiers present: many, several, wide range"
recommendations.change: Where a real bound exists, state it (e.g., "up to N required validations per requirement", specific supported chains like Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base). Otherwise name the concrete examples already implied.
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for generative visibility.

recommendations.title: Add alt text / captions to the four images
recommendations.issue: images carry no textual content an engine can read.
recommendations.change: Add descriptive captions summarizing each diagram (e.g., "CCID links wallet addresses across Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Base to one identity").
recommendations.why: Diagram meaning becomes liftable text rather than an opaque placeholder.

antiPatterns: Untagged code fences (no language hint for parsers).
Four image placeholders with no alt/caption text ("(Image: Image)").
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no broken cross-references — prose is clean.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and og/twitter tags are typically template/site-level — coordinate with the docs platform; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so metadata can be fully verified rather than inferred absent.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good; confirm this page is enumerated there for agent discovery.
Freshness cadence: the body "Last Updated: 2026-07-17" should be mirrored into machine-readable `dateModified`.
